settings.title: Settings
settings.role_primary: Primary: holds the zones and signs them
settings.role_secondary: Secondary: replicates the zones of the primary
settings.primary_exists_title: This cluster already has a primary
settings.primary_exists: {primary} is the primary, so this instance can only be its secondary.
settings.ns_name_helper: The public host name this instance answers as
settings.advertise: Advertise in the NS records of every zone
settings.advertise_helper: Turn off for a hidden server, one that replicates zones but is not listed as a name server
settings.listen_addresses_helper: Addresses of this node to answer DNS queries on. The cluster VPN address {vpn} is always used, for replication.
settings.missing_addresses: Listen addresses not on this node, ignored

zones.title: Zones
zones.zone_name_helper: For example example.com, or 2.0.192.in-addr.arpa for a reverse zone
zones.remove_warning: The zone and its records are deleted, here and on every secondary.
zones.remove_signed_warning: The zone, its records and its DNSSEC keys are deleted, here and on every secondary. If a DS record is still at the registrar, the domain will fail validation: remove it first.
zones.ds_intro: Give this DS record to the registrar, once the name servers are in place:
zones.dnskey_intro: If the registrar asks for the key instead of a DS record, give it this DNSKEY:
zones.ds_warning: The keys are gone. Remove the DS record at the registrar now: until its TTL expires, the domain fails validation.
zones.disable_warning: This deletes the zone's keys. If a DS record is at the registrar, the domain will fail validation: remove it first, and wait for its TTL to expire.
zones.registrar_intro: Enter these at the registrar where {zone} is registered. Until its name servers are there, the internet does not ask this server about the zone.
zones.registrar_intro_reverse: Ask whoever assigned you these addresses, usually your ISP or regional internet registry, to delegate this reverse zone with these entries.
zones.glue_intro: {name} is inside this zone, so the registrar also needs its addresses (glue records):
zones.glue_no_public: {name} is inside this zone, so the registrar needs its public addresses (glue records), and Settings lists none. Give the registrar the public address that reaches this server.
zones.glue_external: {name} is inside this zone and belongs to an external secondary, so the registrar needs its addresses (glue records). Ask the provider for them.
zones.check_no_parent: No server of the parent zone answered.
zones.check_ns_none: The parent zone ({parent}) does not delegate this zone yet.
zones.check_ns_ok: The parent zone ({parent}) lists these name servers.
zones.check_glue_ok: The glue for {name} is in place.
zones.check_glue_bad: Glue for {name}: the parent publishes {published}, and this zone needs {expected}.
zones.check_glue_external_missing: Glue for {name}: the parent publishes none. Give the registrar the addresses the provider gives for it.
zones.check_ds_ok: The DS record is published and matches the zone's key.
zones.check_ds_missing: The parent has no DS record yet, so resolvers do not validate the zone.
zones.check_ds_stale: The parent publishes a DS record that matches no key of this zone, so the domain fails validation. Replace it with the one above.
zones.check_ds_unsigned: The parent publishes a DS record, but this zone is not signed, so the domain fails validation. Remove the DS record at the registrar.
zones.check_ds_unknown: The resolver did not say whether the parent has a DS record.
zones.check_resolve_ok: A validating public resolver ({resolver}) resolves the zone.
zones.check_resolve_servfail: A validating public resolver ({resolver}) fails on the zone. This is most often a DS record that matches no key, or name servers that do not answer.
zones.check_resolve_nxdomain: A public resolver ({resolver}) says the zone does not exist.
zones.check_resolve_error: A public resolver ({resolver}) gave no usable answer for the zone.
zones.check_delay: Changes at the registrar can take up to two days to show here, while the parent zone publishes them and caches expire.

records.title: Records
records.managed: This zone's records are edited in dnshelper.
records.name: Name
records.name_helper: Relative to the zone; @ for the zone itself

replication.title: Replication
replication.no_secondaries_description: Install this module on another node and configure it as a secondary.
replication.remove_description: {module} does not answer. Its entry is removed, its transfer key is revoked and its name server is dropped from the NS records of every zone. Do this only for a secondary that is gone for good: a working secondary is removed with its module, in the Software center.
replication.on_secondary_description: Replication is managed on the primary. See this instance's zones and their transfer state on the Zones page.

external.title: External secondaries
external.intro: Secondary DNS servers outside this cluster, such as a provider's secondary DNS service. They are sent NOTIFY and may transfer the zones they are given, over the internet: TSIG authenticates the transfers but does not encrypt them, and the provider sees every record of those zones and every query for them.
external.none_description: Add one to have a server outside the cluster serve some or all of your zones.
external.name: Name
external.name_helper: A label for this list, such as the provider's name
external.notify_helper: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, one per line, that the provider tells you to send NOTIFY to. They are often not the addresses of its name servers.
external.ns_names_helper: The provider's name servers, one per line, such as ns1.provider.example. Leave empty if it is not to answer for your zones publicly.
external.advertise: Advertise these name servers in the NS records of the zones it receives
external.zones_all: All zones, including zones added later
external.auth_ip: Source address only, for providers that cannot use TSIG
external.ip_warning_title: Transfers are allowed by address alone
external.ip_warning: Anyone who can send from these addresses can read every record of the zones given to this secondary. Use TSIG if the provider offers it.
external.transfer_from_helper: The addresses or networks the provider transfers from, one per line. A network can be no wider than /24 for IPv4 or /48 for IPv6.
external.key_generate_new: Generate a new key, revoking the current one
external.key_paste: Use a key issued by the provider, revoking the current one
external.key_paste_new: Use a key issued by the provider
external.key_name_helper: Leave empty for powerdns-<id>, unless the provider dictates a name.
external.secret_helper: The base64 secret the provider gave you.
external.key_intro: Enter this key at the provider, so that its transfers are signed with it. Anyone with the secret can read the zones given to this secondary: keep it private.
external.remove_description: {name} will no longer be notified or allowed to transfer any zone, its key is revoked, and its name servers are dropped from the NS records of the zones it was given. Update the registrar of those zones if its name servers were listed there.

dns_status.standby: This is a copy of the primary {other}. It serves its zones but takes no changes. It takes over when that primary is removed.
dns_status.two_primaries: {other} is also registered as a primary. Remove one of them.
dns_status.not_configured: Choose the role of this instance in Settings.
dns_status.waiting: {other} on this node holds port 53, so this copy is not serving. It starts within a minute of that instance being removed.
